To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mechanism of L7/L2 ribosomal stalk subunit exchange is via L7/L2 monomers and dimer and binding of EF-G to the ribosome reduces the rate of L7/L8 subunit exchange.

(1) the exchange of ribosomal L7/L12 proceeds via monomers and dimeters and (2) binding of elongation factor G to the posttranslocation ribosome reduces the rate of L7/L1 exchange by ~27% for monomers and ~47% for dimers.
L7/L12 is exchanged between ribosomes via monomers and dimes, and binding of EF-G slows down the exchange.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how proteins interact with the ribosome.
the ribosome, the cellular machine responsible for protein synthesis.
the mechanism and regulation of protein synthesis in Escherichia col.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the exchange of the ribosomal stalk proteins is a dynamic and regulated process that is modulated by the binding of translation factors.
the exchange of L12 subunits from ribosomal stalk occurs through a monomer-dimer mechanism and the binding of EF-G inhibits the exchange of L2 monomers and dimmers from the ribosomal stalk.
the exchange of L12 is not affected by the binding of EF-G but the exchange of L11 is slowed down by 2-fold.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the L7/L 12 exchange is a dynamic process that is regulated by the presence of the ribosome-bound translation factors.
the ribosomal stalk proteins are highly dynamic and that their exchange is regulated by binding of the translation factor EF-G.
the ribosomal L7/L12 proteins are highly dynamic and that the ribosome has a mechanism to modulate the dynamics of the L7/L2 stalk complex in response to binding of translation factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
L7/L12 is not an immutable part of the ribosome and that the stability of this protein is regulated by the binding of EF-G.
binding of EF G does not affect the exchange of L12 monomers but it does reduce exchange of L12 dimers by ~50%.
the exchange of L12 from the ribosome is a dynamic process that can be modulated by the binding of EF-G to the ribosome, and the exchange of L11 is a much slower process.
